title: A5 fixpipe scaled casts to BF16, FP32, E4M3 and HiFloat8 straight from L0C to GM
surface: Tensor.requant(scale=) on an FP32 or INT32 L0C accumulator stored directly into a GM tensor of the destination dtype -- bfloat16, float32, float8_e4m3fn and UINT8 HiFloat8 carriers under two rounding policies -- with no UB staging; one kernel(mode="cube") launch per conversion
study_for: The cube operands are FP16 and the HiFloat8 encoders consume the *FP32* L0C value after the scale. The accumulator's width is not the operands' width, and these two outputs are where that distinction is observable rather than notional.

`hif8_ta` and `hif8_hybrid` are the same value under two rounding policies, and `check_domain` refuses a case in which the two references agree everywhere -- otherwise the pair that exists to distinguish the policies would be two copies of one check.

`scaled_f32` is the control the two casts are read against: the same scaled accumulator, kept at full width. It is also the only output with a tolerance, and for a stated reason -- the host product is FP64 while the device accumulates in FP32 in its own order, so the bound covers the accumulation and not the conversion. The five carrier outputs have no tolerance at all.

The scalar scale is truncated to the top 19 FP32 bits before it is applied. 0.5 is exact under that truncation and `check_domain` asserts it, so the truncation changes no value here while the rule stays stated for a scale where it would.

`boundaries` plants products on each format's seams rather than sampling near them: the E4M3 lattice edges 448 and 464, BF16 rounding ties, powers of two down to 2**-22, and one value chosen to be the exact FP32 predecessor of 16 after the product and the scale. A generated case cannot be relied on to land on any of those.

`corrected` is the only case whose products are not exact -- Gaussian FP16 operands at the corrected helper's own M32 N64 K64 geometry. Keeping it alongside the two exact cases is what separates 'the conversion is right' from 'the conversion is right on exactly representable values'.
do_not_copy_when: Your operands are not finite and bounded by 1024 in FP16. That bound is what keeps the FP32 accumulation and the format conversions inside their stated domains, and it is checked.
Your scale is not exact under the FP19 truncation. Then the truncation is part of the answer and needs its own reference; nothing here establishes how an arbitrary scale rounds.
You expect one HiFloat8 rounding policy to stand for the other. They are separate entries because they differ, and a case where they did not differ is refused.

You want the other direct-GM modes on this device. Five more live in the `cube_quant` example at its own pin, and the L0C-to-UB arrangement is `cube_quant_ub`. Neither establishes this path, and this one establishes neither of theirs.

You are reading `scaled_f32`'s tolerance as a conversion tolerance. It covers the FP32 accumulation order against an FP64 host product; the conversions themselves are compared as carriers with no room at all.
